title: Add benchmark report landing page copy + disclaimers + methodology summary
author: Wei Chen
release_notes: Marketing site: new /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar landing page with methodology summary, disclosure language, and links to full report + reproducibility artifacts.
body:
## Summary
Adds the initial public landing page for the Latency-per-dollar benchmark report, including legally-reviewed disclaimers, a short methodology summary, and links to the full PDF + interactive table (coming in subsequent PR). This PR is copy/content + basic layout wiring only; no benchmark numbers are embedded here (those will be served via the benchmark results service + data artifacts).

## Why
We need a single canonical page to:
- Explain what “latency/$” means and how to interpret it.
- Set expectations for variance, region availability, model versioning, and workload fit.
- Provide guardrails on comparative language (avoid implying “best overall” or universal superiority).
- Give Sales/SEs and Support a stable URL to link when prospects ask “how did you measure this?”

## What’s included
- New docs/marketing page: /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar
- Methodology summary (high-level, non-technical audience), with explicit link to the full methodology document.
- Disclaimers / disclosures section:
  - Metric definition (latency/$ is normalized and depends on workload + pricing assumptions)
  - Run conditions (regions, concurrency, warmups, caching policy described at a high level)
  - Variance/stability caveats (p95 sensitivity, queueing effects, capacity variability)
  - Model version + configuration disclosure (pinning, quantization profile note)
  - Comparative-claims language (no “fastest everywhere”; no “X% cheaper than competitor” in body copy)
  - Trademarks and third-party references caveat
- CTA wiring to: Download PDF, View interactive results (placeholder until PR-3924/benchmarks data ingestion lands), and “Try Redwood” signup.

## Out of scope
- Publishing the PDF asset (tracked in PR-3924)
- Interactive table + filters (tracked separately; will pull JSON artifacts from results service)
- Any new benchmark runs or number changes

## Review checklist
- [x] PMM review for narrative & positioning (Soojin)
- [x] Product review for accuracy (Henry)
- [x] Legal review for claims/disclaimer completeness (Michael/Sofia)
- [x] Security review for operational detail leakage (Naomi)
- [x] Accessibility spot-check (Alicia)

## Notes / decisions
- We use “latency per dollar” and “latency/$” interchangeably but always define it the first time on-page.
- We avoid competitor names in headings and keep any third-party references confined to a neutral “context” paragraph.
- We explicitly state that results are not a guarantee of performance for every workload and encourage users to run a PoC.

## Screenshots
Included in commit as a lightweight local preview screenshot (no benchmark figures).

## Follow-ups
- Add interactive table content + data ingestion (PM-826)
- Publish PDF & assets (PR-3924)
- Add cross-links from API performance docs and Sales enablement FAQ (PR-3931 / enablement updates)

---

### Changed areas (high level)
- site/pages/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar.mdx (new)
- site/components/BenchmarkDisclaimers.tsx (new)
- site/components/Callouts/DisclosureCallout.tsx (new)
- site/styles/benchmarks.css (new)
- site/content/legal/benchmark-disclosures.md (new source-of-truth copy block)
- site/nav.ts (add route)
- site/redirects.json (add legacy alias)

### Illustrative snippet (disclaimer block excerpt)
We include a standardized disclosure block: “Benchmark results reflect the specific workloads, model versions, and regions described in the Methodology. Latency and cost can vary based on prompt distribution, concurrency, caching behavior, and regional capacity. Results are provided for informational purposes and should not be interpreted as a performance guarantee.”

## Commits
1) docs(benchmarks): add landing page scaffold + nav route
2) docs(benchmarks): add methodology summary section + links
3) docs(legal): add benchmark disclosures + comparative language constraints
4) ui: add disclosure callout component + styling
5) chore: redirects + link check fixes

## CI
- build-docs: PASS
- lint: PASS
- typecheck: PASS
- link-check: PASS
- visual-regression (baseline): PASS

## Review conversation (selected)
Soojin Lee (PMM): “Can we remove ‘best-in-class’ and replace with something measurable? Also please add a short paragraph on who this benchmark is for (production inference economics) vs raw model quality.”
Wei Chen (author): Updated hero + subhead to remove subjective phrasing; added ‘What this benchmark measures’ section + explicit scope statement.

Michael Grant (Legal): “We need a clearer separation between (1) our methodology claims and (2) any comparative implications. Also add a disclaimer that third-party trademarks belong to their owners and that we’re not affiliated/endorsed.”
Wei Chen: Added ‘Comparative language’ subsection + trademark sentence; moved any comparative framing to a neutral ‘How to interpret’ section.

Sofia Mendes (Legal): “Please avoid ‘faster everywhere’/‘cheaper everywhere’ language. Also add explicit note that pricing assumptions and configuration choices impact latency/$.”
Wei Chen: Removed absolute language; added pricing/config dependence note; added link to methodology appendix.

Henry Cho (Product): “Methodology summary should mention prefill/decode mix at a high level, and state that caching is controlled/consistent across runs (without implying customers will automatically get the same).”
Wei Chen: Added two bullets: prefill+decode representation and caching policy controlled during runs; added ‘your mileage may vary’ line.

Naomi Feldman (Security): “Don’t include internal region capacity notes or instance identifiers. The current wording is fine; keep it high level (cloud region names only).”
Wei Chen: Removed reference to instance family; kept region list generic.

Alicia Perez (Design/UX): “Disclosure callout is dense on mobile; can we collapse/expand and ensure keyboard accessibility?”
Wei Chen: Added <details>/<summary> pattern with proper focus styles and ARIA labeling.

Approvals:
- Soojin Lee: Approved
- Michael Grant: Approved with final wording noted in comment
- Sofia Mendes: Approved
- Henry Cho: Approved
- Naomi Feldman: Approved
- Alicia Perez: Approved

## Merge
Squash merged to main after approvals + CI green. Post-merge: site deploy verified in staging (benchmarks route accessible; link-check clean).
